subject: cat
readings: head at +x: XY panel is the profile, ZY is the front view of the face/chest, XZ is a top-down view
ears/head top (20-23,4) in XY, nose (24,8) in XY -> head sits at far +x, small and forward
withers/neck junction (15,7) in XY; neck base (17,6); these are close in x,y confirming a short thick neck
pelvis/rump (9,13) in XY; spine curves from pelvis (9,13) up to withers (15,7) giving a rising back line
tail base at rump (2,11) in XY, tail tip after curl (1,16) in XY -> tail length ~7 to a curled tip
front shoulder top (15,8) in XY and (15,8),z=13/7 in ZY, front paw (15,20) in both panels -> front leg span 12
hind hip (9,13) in XY, hind knee (7,17), hind paw (7,20) -> hind leg bends back then down, span ~7 vertical but longer path due to bend
ZY panel: two front legs spread at z~13 (right) and z~7 (left), shoulders at y~8, paws at y~20-24, elbows visible mid-way at y~14
ZY panel: hind legs at z~14 (right) and z~6 (left), hips near pelvis y~13, knees y~17, paws y~20
ground line at y=20 in XY/ZY matches paw positions, confirming legs reach the same ground level
notes: Head faces +x, so the XY panel is the profile view (used for x,y of spine, tail, and vertical leg extents); the ZY panel supplies the z (left/right) split for the paired legs, with +z assigned to the animal's right per the right-hand frame (x forward, y up). Spine is split into pelvis->spine_mid->withers->neck->head as inferred anatomical segments (only two hard landmarks - withers and neck junction - were directly visible, the spine_mid was inferred to keep the spine as multiple internal nodes rather than one hub). Each leg is split into hip/shoulder->knee/elbow->paw, with knee/elbow positions inferred from the visible bend in both XY and ZY panels rather than being explicit landmarks. Front and hind legs are each authored as two independent full chains from pelvis or withers to their own paw leaf, per the two-frame chain rule. Tail is a single 2-segment flap (base+tip) reflecting its curled shape. All four legs are encoded with equal proportional length pairs (front pair equal, hind pair equal) despite the mid-stride pose making them look uneven on screen.
